own_solution.law: Doppler effect, moving source, stationary observer, still air: f' = f c/(c - v_s)
assumptions: source moves directly toward listener (approaching phase)

defect_reasons.other: The R sentences rely on temporal wording ('then tuned up', 'just before the tone was measured') against a 'steady tone' of 440 Hz 'when first switched on', so the moment at which the heard frequency is asked is only implied (after retuning).

notes: Checked: base 440*343/323 = 467.245 Hz; R answers 449*343/323 = 476.802, 456*343/323 = 484.235, 464*343/323 = 492.731 Hz, all correct. The C cancellation is correct: t2 - t1 = 1/f - vs/(f c) = (c - vs)/(f c), independent of d; all listed distances (180, 300, 950 m) keep the siren in the approaching phase for at least one period. In pass 1 I labelled the distance K (approach regime); the authors' C derivation, with d appearing in the arrival-time relations and cancelling, is valid, so I accept C. Minimal pairs T5688/T8B99 (violin vs siren, 16 Hz) and TEE83/TD410 (earlier run vs just before measurement, 16 Hz) share number and unit and differ only in attachment. Numeral-free twins TEDCB and T62DC match their D twins with the number replaced. Distance sentences TE5DD and T4EE7 both state 300 m. No contradictions found; 'steady tone' plus a retuning is a mild wording tension, not a contradiction, given the clause about the tone at switch-on.
